clue.text: Sweet that's lavish in nuts

indicators.note: in tells us one word is placed inside the other, splitting the crazy word before its last letter

parts.note: nuts, meaning crazy, is bananas in slang
to lavish money is to fritter it, so fritters is the verb form

explanation.surface: A pudding described as generous with its nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lavish' reads as an adjective describing the sweet, but it works as a verb, as in lavishing or frittering away money.
explanation.definitionFit: Fried battered fruit slices are a dessert, so a sweet in the British sense of a pudding.

clue.text: Ship's watch seeks a profitable catch

definitions.note: the definition describes what the person does rather than naming them: one who seeks a profitable catch

parts.note: the Bounty is the famous ship of the 1789 mutiny
a hunter is a pocket watch with a hinged cover protecting the face

explanation.surface: A ship's timepiece goes looking for a lucrative haul.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Ship's' just joins the two pieces. A hunter watch has a metal lid over its glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A person tracking outlaws for the reward money is chasing a capture that pays.

clue.text: Clothes of many Londoners contain this

definitions.text: Clothes of many Londoners contain this

indicators.note: contain says the words many Londoners hold the required letters across their join

explanation.surface: A remark that city dwellers' garments include a certain synthetic.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'maNY LONdoners'. The whole clue is also the definition: plenty of clothing is made of this synthetic fibre.
explanation.definitionFit: This synthetic fibre is used in a great deal of everyday clothing, so many people's garments include it.

clue.text: Enthusiast about to reduce measure of food

indicators.note: about means the enthusiast's letters go round the others

parts.note: a nut is a fan or enthusiast, as in a fitness nut
to trim something is to reduce it
an en is a printer's measure of width

explanation.surface: A fan is about to cut down a portion of food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'measure of food' looks like one phrase, but 'measure' is the printer's unit and 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Nourishing substance is food in a formal or scientific sense.

clue.text: Charge for carrying soldier into battle

indicators.note: into tells us the soldier goes inside the battle word

parts.note: a battle is a fight
RE is the Royal Engineers, the British army corps, so a soldier from it

explanation.surface: An accusation is laid for bringing a soldier into combat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' looks like an accusation, but here it is a fee. RE, the Royal Engineers, is a common crossword soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Freight can mean the fee paid for transporting goods as well as the goods themselves.

clue.text: Approve hunter following deer without aspiration

indicators.note: aspiration is the breathy sound of an initial H, so both words drop that letter, as a dropped-aitch speaker would
following says the hunter word comes after the deer word

parts.note: a hind is a female deer
a hunter is a horse bred for riding to hounds

explanation.surface: Giving the nod to a huntsman who is trailing a deer, said breathlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without aspiration' removes the H from each word: HIND becomes IND, HORSE becomes ORSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Indorse is a variant spelling of endorse, which means to approve or back.

clue.text: Highwayman powerless in Italy

definitions.note: the definition means a place found in Italy

indicators.note: powerless means without power, whose standard physics abbreviation is P, so that letter is removed

parts.note: Dick Turpin was a notorious English highwayman of the 1730s

explanation.surface: A robber of the roads finds himself without power in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'powerless' removes P, the abbreviation for power, from TURPIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin is a large city in the north-west of Italy, capital of Piedmont.

clue.text: Catch the Italian in trip over the roof

definitions.note: the definition describes where the item sits rather than naming it

indicators.note: in says the first pieces go inside the trip word

parts.note: a trip is a ride
to catch something is to get it
il is the Italian word for the

explanation.surface: Catching an Italian man while on a journey across the rooftops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catch' and 'trip' look like a stumble, but they are get and ride; the definition describes where the tile sits.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge tile is the curved tile laid along the apex of a roof, covering it at the top.

clue.text: Empty university accommodation finally gets grant

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word accommodation

parts.note: to let is to allow or grant

explanation.surface: Vacant student housing at last gets its funding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grant' looks like student funding, but it is the verb meaning allow.
explanation.definitionFit: A property not rented out is vacant, so empty.

clue.text: Adore old ruin in the land of opportunity

indicators.note: to ruin the words is to wreck their letter order

explanation.surface: Someone loves an old ruin in a country of chances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruin' looks like a noun for a crumbling building, but it is a verb telling us to shuffle ADOREOLD.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary city of gold stands for any place where riches and opportunity abound.

clue.text: Game Chinese gangs engaged in, modifying locks

definitions.note: the definition describes the tool by its job, changing the shape of hair

parts.note: curling is a sport played by sliding stones on ice
tongs are Chinese secret societies or gangs

explanation.surface: A sport that Chinese gangs took part in, changing the locks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engaged in' is a link joining the two pieces. 'locks' suggests doors, but here it means hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A heated hair tool for making curls is used to restyle locks of hair.

clue.text: Cure Rex after defeat

parts.note: to cure leather is to tan it
rex is Latin for king, as in the royal cipher

explanation.surface: Treatment for Rex following a loss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cure' suggests medicine, but it is the leather-working sense. 'after' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanking is informal for a heavy defeat, as when a team goes down badly.

clue.text: Our dean composed a poem

indicators.note: composed suggests the letters have been put together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A college dean wrote some verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' fits the poem in the surface, but it signals rearranging OURDEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondeau is a French verse form with a refrain, so a particular kind of poem.

clue.text: Bears note for dispatch

parts.note: to bear a thing is to have it, so bears gives has
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Large animals send a message to be sent off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bears' looks like the animals, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Dispatch can mean speed or promptness, a synonym of hurry.

clue.text: Bear guest destroying plant

indicators.note: destroying says the original order of these letters is wrecked

explanation.surface: A bear wrecks a visitor's crop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroying' rearranges BEARGUEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar beet is a crop grown for its sugar-rich root, so a plant.

clue.text: Time to study philosopher? That's dreary!

definitions.note: the definition is an exclamation describing a monotonous routine, which the answer names

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university
John Stuart Mill was a 19th-century English philosopher

explanation.surface: Time to read a thinker? What a bore!
explanation.walkthrough: Reading a subject is the British phrase for studying it at university.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadmill is figuratively a tedious, repetitive grind, the very image of monotony.

clue.text: Ruin a street that's shady

parts.note: to dish someone's chances is to ruin them
a means one

explanation.surface: A ruined street that is in shadow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruin a street' looks like an anagram of A STREET, but that gives only seven letters. 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Shady describes a dubious, untrustworthy person or deal, a synonym of crooked.

clue.text: Show venue close to centre of constable's beat

parts.note: nigh means near or close

indicators.note: centre of picks the middle letter of the nine-letter word constable

parts.note: to club someone is to beat them

explanation.surface: Near the middle of a policeman's patrol area is a place for performances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat' looks like a police patrol route, but it is the verb. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightclub is a venue for late-night entertainment, including cabaret shows.

clue.text: Teaching flower arrangement for rock singer?

parts.note: lore is traditional teaching or knowledge
a lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers

explanation.surface: Instruction in floristry for a rock musician?
explanation.walkthrough: The Lorelei is a Rhine rock where, in legend, a siren sang sailors to their doom: hence 'rock singer' with its question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: In German legend a siren sat on the Lorelei rock singing, luring boatmen onto it.

clue.text: Oxford University official's encyclical upset the Almighty

parts.note: a papal bull is a formal letter from the Pope, as an encyclical is

indicators.note: in a down answer upset means turned upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the Almighty is God

explanation.surface: A college officer's papal letter angered God.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'official's' is a link. 'upset' looks like 'angered' but reverses GOD to DOG.
explanation.definitionFit: At Oxford a bulldog is a proctor's attendant who helps keep university order.

clue.text: Rear small bird

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: Raising a tiny bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rear' looks like the verb to bring up, but it is the back of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The stern is the rear part of a ship.

clue.text: Noble queen toured island previously

parts.note: an earl is a nobleman
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: An aristocrat and a monarch went round an island some time ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toured' means went around: the island letter goes inside the queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Earlier means at a prior time, a synonym of before.

clue.text: I rent accommodation in Bury

indicators.note: accommodation suggests adapting or adjusting, so the letters are rearranged to fit

explanation.surface: Renting a flat in a Lancashire town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accommodation' signals a rearrangement of IRENT. 'Bury', a town near Manchester, wants to be a place name, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter a body is to bury it.

clue.text: Brute captures good old sentry

indicators.note: captures means the brute's letters hold the others inside

parts.note: a lout is a brutish oaf
OK means all right or good

explanation.surface: A thug seizes a decent elderly guard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good old' looks like an affectionate phrase, but each word gives its own abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A person keeping watch is a guard, so a sentry.

clue.text: Bird betrayed by Toulouse-Lautrec

indicators.note: betrayed by means given away by, so the letters are revealed within the painter's name

explanation.surface: A bird gives itself away in a painter's work.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit in 'tOULOUSE-Lautrec'.
explanation.definitionFit: The ousel is an old name for the blackbird, or the ring ousel, a thrush.

clue.text: Try Leeds converted generated new manner

indicators.note: converted means changed in form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fans in a Yorkshire city were won round to a new way of doing things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' signals a rearrangement of TRYLEEDS. Leeds is a city in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: To restyle something is to give it a fresh style or fashion, so produce a new manner.

clue.text: Weaken when losing pounds in Germany

definitions.note: the definition means a place found in Germany

indicators.note: when losing says the money letter is dropped from the weakening word

parts.note: to weaken something is to lessen it
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Something weakens as it loses money in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' removes L from LESSEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is an industrial city in the Ruhr region of western Germany.

clue.text: Jumping hedges on the racecourse

definitions.note: the definition describes where the gates are found rather than naming them

parts.note: starting means jumping in surprise
to hedge is to stall or evade a question

explanation.surface: Leaping over hedges at a horse-racing track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hedges' and 'Jumping' suggest steeplechase fences, but they are the verbs evades and startling.
explanation.definitionFit: Starting stalls are the gated boxes from which horses begin a flat race.
